sentences.text:
Ms. Geetanjali Chourasiya - Govt. Advocate For The
 Respondent/State.
ORDER Heard on admission as well as on I.A.No.9945/2024 filed for exemption from surrender.

2. This criminal revision under Section 397 read with Section 401 of Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 (hereinafter referred as, 'Cr.P.C.') has been filed by the applicant against the order dated 22/05/2024 passed in Cr.A.No.32/2023 by 29 th Additional Sessions Judge, Indore (M.P.)
dismissing the appeal preferred against the order dated 22/12/2022 passed in Criminal Case No.2617417/2008 by Special Magistrate, Municipal Corporation, Indore, wherein the applicant was convicted for the offence under Section 7(i) read with Section 16(1)(A)(i) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and sentenced to under go Rigorous Imprisonment of 06 months with fine of Rs.1,000/-.

3. Learned counsel for the applicant placing reliance on the order dated 29/08/2022 passed in Criminal Revision No.3048/2022 (Tapan Sen Vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh) by the co-ordinate Bench of this Court at Jabalpur submits that the applicant is suffering from various ailments and therefore, was not able to surrender before the trial Court for undergoing the sentence as imposed by the trial Court and affirmed by the appellate Court.

entities.text: Criminal Revision No.3048/2022 (Tapan Sen Vs. The State of Madhya Pradesh)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel further submits that surrendering of the applicant before the trial Court for entertaining the criminal revision is not mandatory.
On these grounds, learned counsel prays for allowing the application for exemption from surrender and to admit the criminal revision.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent / State has opposed the prayer by referring Rule 48 of the High Court of Madhya Pradesh Rules, 2008.

entities.text: High Court of Madhya Pradesh Rules, 2008
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
She has also placed reliance on the order Mahesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 2 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5205292/
1 passed by the co-ordinate Bench of this Court at Indore in the matter of Devnarayan and Others Vs.
Prateek Goyanka (passed in Criminal Revision No.1912/2024 on 28/05/2024).

entities.text: Mahesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
Devnarayan and Others Vs.
Prateek Goyanka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On these contentions, she prays for dismissal of application along with the criminal revision as it is not maintainable without surrender of the applicant.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.

For ready reference, Rule 48 of the High Court of Madhya Pradesh Rules, 2008 reads as under:-
"48. A memorandum of appeal or revision petition against conviction, except in cases where the sentence has been suspended by the Court below, shall contain a declaration to the effect that the convicted person is in custody or has surrendered after the conviction."
7. The co-ordinate Bench of this Court relying upon the judgments passed by the apex Court in Deepak Sahu Vs. State of M.P. Reported in 2012 (3) MPLJ 534 / 2012 SCC OnLine MP 808 and Vivek Rai and another Vs. State of Jharkhand reported in (2015) 12 SCC 86 has passed an order in Devnarayan (Supra), para 11 of the same reads as under:-
"11.

entities.text: High Court of Madhya Pradesh Rules, 2008
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Deepak Sahu Vs. State of M.P. Reported in 2012 (3) MPLJ 534 / 2012 SCC OnLine MP 808
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Vivek Rai and another Vs. State of Jharkhand reported in (2015) 12 SCC 86
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, it is apparent that although it is not mandatory that a convict must surrender at the time of filing of Criminal Revision, but to claim the exemption from the same, he has to demonstrate the exceptional circumstances as has been held by the Supreme Court in the aforesaid case of Vivek Rai (supra), and in the absence of the same, a person cannot claim as a matter of right, that he is not required to surrender before the District Appellate Court before filing the criminal revision in the High Court, and since no such grounds have been raised by the petitioner, this Court is of the considered opinion that the petitioner is required to surrender before the District Appellate Court before his criminal revision is taken up for hearing."
8.

The order relied upon by the applicant in Tapan Sen (Supra) has been given in the peculiar factual matrix of its own case, therefore, it cannot be treated as a precedent and more so it does not mandate that each and every case in which special circumstance has been shown, the applicant will be treated in the way treated in Tapan Sen (Supra)'s case.

9. In light of the aforesaid discussion, when the applicant in the instant case could not satisfy this Court that there were some special circumstances due to which he could not surrender before the trial Court, exemption from surrender cannot be granted in light of the Rule 48 of M.P. High Court Rules, 2008 as mentioned herein above.
10. In absence of declaration to the effect that applicant is in custody, this criminal revision is not maintainable
, therefore, I.A.No.9945/2024 stands dismissed and as a consequence the criminal revision also stands dismissed being not maintainable.
Certified copy as per rules.
